title: cldr liberator: install matthewsinclair/cldr/cldr and link ~/.config/cldr from the user repo's config/cldr
body:
## What

A `cldr` liberator. cldr (`~/Devel/prj/Cldr`, public; replaces the journal's `bin/journal`) reads its config from `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cldr/config.toml`. hv's config decides the numbers (dated zones, tag spellings, what counts as work, billable fractions), so it is versioned in Molt-matts at `config/cldr/config.toml` (private) and linked into place, as menuz's is.

hv, 1 Nov 2026: "You'll need a new liberator for cldr and we'll also need to make a homebrew-cldr repo on Git for the brew process." On where the config lives: "Linked into the XFG_* dirs?" (yes).

## Next

1. `liberators/cldr.sh`, two halves:
   - Homebrew, as `intent.sh`: `molt_brew_faults` / `molt_brew_install` for `matthewsinclair/cldr/cldr` (the tap is `matthewsinclair/homebrew-cldr`; the formula builds from the tag's source).
   - Config, as `menuz.sh`: link the whole `~/.config/cldr` directory to the user repo's `config/cldr`, only when that directory exists (an editor's save can replace a linked file with a plain copy, so the directory is linked, not the file). Respect `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` when set and absolute.
2. A bats test beside `test/liberators/menuz.bats`; README's liberator list; CHANGELOG.
3. Enable it in `instances/rhadamanth/molt.toml` (macOS; cldr also builds on Linux, so the liberator need not be macOS-only, but only rhadamanth needs it now).

## State when filed

- Molt-matts `config/cldr/config.toml` holds hv's config; `~/.config/cldr` on rhadamanth is linked to it by hand until this liberator owns the link.
- `brew install matthewsinclair/cldr/cldr` works once the tap repo exists on GitHub and v0.1.0 is released (`tools/release` in Cldr). Until then the Homebrew half has nothing to install.
- cldr needs Full Disk Access for the terminal to read BusyCal's store; that is the terminal's grant, not Molt's to make. `cldr doctor` reports it.

Molt's builders start only when hv calls Molt.
